Event of Default, Landlord may terminate this Lease, re-enter and relet the Leased Premises without terminating, and recover all damages permitted by law, including rent deficiencies, default interest, attorneys’ fees, and the unamortized cost of tenant improvements, rent abatement, and leasing commissions. Landlord shall use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate damages, but shall not be required to prioritize the Leased Premises over other vacancies, accept below-market terms, or alter the intended use or character of the building. Tenant shall have no right to offset, deduct, counterclaim, or withhold rent.

Tenant covenants and agrees: (a) to maintain all licenses and permits required for Tenant’s medical operations; (b) upon expiration or termination of this Lease, to remove its personal property and effects and to surrender the Leased Premises to Landlord in accordance with Article XVII; (c) to comply with all applicable laws relating to Tenant’s specific use and occupancy of the Leased Premises, including applicable healthcare licensure and patient privacy laws; and (d) Tenant’s use will not exceed the floor load, electrical, plumbing, water, or exhaust capacity allocated to the Leased Premises, and will not interfere with other tenants through vibration, odor, noise, or radiofrequency interference with adjacent diagnostic equipment.

Section 3.  HIPAA.  Landlord acknowledges that Tenant’s operations at the Leased Premises are subject to the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996, as amended (“HIPAA”), and agrees that neither Landlord nor its employees, agents, or contractors shall access, review, or remove any patient records or protected health information that may be present at the Leased Premises, and shall comply with Tenant’s reasonable HIPAA-related access protocols described in Section 4 of Article IX.

Section 3.  HIPAA.  Tenant shall secure all patient records and protected health information so that Landlord’s exercise of ordinary landlord rights does not result in disclosure. Landlord and its employees, agents, and contractors shall not intentionally access, review, copy, or remove such information. The parties do not intend to create a business-associate relationship, and Landlord shall not be deemed a business associate under HIPAA solely by performing its obligations or exercising its rights under this Lease. Incidental disclosure during permitted access shall not constitute a breach by Landlord.

Contractor shall conduct himself or herself at all times with due regard to public morals and conventions. If at any time during the Term of this Agreement, Contractor conducts himself or herself in a manner offensive to decency, morality or social propriety resulting in scandal or ridicule, or that reflects unfavorably on Company, Company’s products or the image of the Company’s “brand,” or that materially reduces the value of Company’s association with Contractor, Company shall have the right in its sole reasonable good faith discretion to immediately terminate this Agreement. If Contractor publicly disparages Company, its brands or its products Company shall also have the right to immediately terminate this Agreement. In addition, upon written request by Company at any time, Contractor agrees that it shall remove, within twelve (12) hours of such request, or by the end of the same business day where the request cites a legal or regulatory demand, all content and communications from its social media pages, its websites or other outlets that contain Company’s intellectual property or that refer to Company, the Company Property or any Company product, and shall keep such content down and not repost it. Contractor shall preserve a copy of each such Post and its available analytics for twelve (12) months following removal. This obligation shall survive the expiration or termination of this Agreement.

During the Term, Company may, after the process below, terminate this Agreement only if Contractor (a) is convicted of, or pleads guilty or nolo contendere to, a felony or crime involving moral turpitude; (b) is charged with an offense involving violence or the safety of a minor; (c) engages in hate speech or unlawful harassment; (d) is banned from Instagram or TikTok for a material breach of applicable community standards; or (e) engages in conduct that becomes the subject of widespread public condemnation in national media. Before terminating, Company shall give Contractor written notice describing the conduct in reasonable detail, allow Contractor five (5) business days to respond, and confer in good faith regarding the notice. Pending that process, Company may require the Posts to be made private; if the notice is not sustained, the Fee remains unaffected. Unsubstantiated allegations, conduct occurring before the Effective Date, and Contractor’s good-faith expression of personal, political or religious views shall not trigger this paragraph. Neither party shall publicly disparage the other during the Term, except for truthful statements made in a dispute or to professional advisers. In addition, upon Company’s written request identifying a legal or regulatory requirement, platform action, licensor demand, or product-safety concern, Contractor shall remove or make private only the Post(s) created under this SOW within five (5) business days, except that a request identifying a genuine legal or regulatory requirement or product-safety concern shall be actioned by the end of the same business day. This obligation does not extend to Contractor’s organic content or content created for any prior or other campaign, ends upon expiration or termination of this SOW, and does not reduce the Fee if Company requests removal before the end of the ninety (90)-day live period. Contractor shall preserve a copy of each such Post and its available analytics for twelve (12) months following removal.
